item.title: Bronze Medalist
item.description: Tonga has ended a 16-year Commonwealth Games medal drought after heavyweight judoka Paula Monta claimed a historic bronze medal in the men's +100kg competition at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games. Paula Monta became Tonga's first and only medalist of the Commonwelath Games since 2010 after defeating Canada's John Messe Bessong in a hard-fought bronze medal contest.
item.content:encoded:
Tonga has ended a 16-year Commonwealth Games medal drought after heavyweight judoka Paula Monta claimed a historic bronze medal in the men's +100kg competition at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games.

Paula Monta became Tonga's first and only medalist of the Commonwelath Games since 2010 after defeating Canada's John Messe Bessong in a hard-fought bronze medal contest.

The encounter went the full distance, with Monta holding off a late challenge from the Canadian Judoka to secure victory by the narrowest of margins. He prevailed with one waza-ari and two yuko to Bessong's one waza-ari and one yuko.

The bronze medal is a remarkable campaign for the 21-year-old, who fought his way through the repechage after an earlier defeat to earn another chance at the podium before delivering under pressure in the medal playoff.

The result ends the nation's 16-year wait for a Commonwealth Games medal and providing Team Tonga with its first podium finish of the Glasgow Games.

Monta's success follows months of preparation in Japan under the guidance of coach Josateki Naulu, the former Fiji international judoka and Olympian. The Tonga Judo Association credited Naulu's dedication and expertise as instrumental in preparing Monta for the historic performance.

In recognition of his achievement, Monta was also named Tonga's flag bearer for Team Tonga in the Commonwealth Games closing ceremony.

The Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games officially concluded on Sunday, August 2, 2026, with a vibrant closing ceremony inside the OVO Hydro arena in Glasgow, Scotland. The 11-day sporting event wrapped up with musical performances, athlete parades, and the formal handover of the Commonwealth Games flag to the next host city.

Amdavad (Ahmedabad), India, will host the Centenary Games in 2030.

item.title: Members question govt before House adjourns
item.description: Questions were raised over seriously delayed government projects, including the Fanga'uta Lagoon Bridge, before the House adjourned for next week. The Prime Minister said that the required land documentation had not been completed. To address the delays, responsibility for the land-related aspects of the project had been transferred from the Ministry of Lands to the Prime Minister's Office ( PMO )
item.content:encoded:
Questions were raised over seriously delayed government projects, including the Fanga'uta Lagoon Bridge, before the House adjourned for next week.

The Prime Minister said that the required land documentation had not been completed. To address the delays, responsibility for the land-related aspects of the project had been transferred from the Ministry of Lands to the Prime Minister's Office ( PMO ). He acknowledged that "project management issues" contributed to the delays.

Meanwhile, two bills passed first readings, and nine Annual Reports from Ministries were tabled into Parliament and referred to the Whole House Committee.

The Acting Minister for Finance, PM Lord Fakafanua tabled two Bills into the House when it was reconvened on Monday, 3 August.

The Payment Systems for Services Bill 2026 will help people because electronic payment systems will be easier and cheaper and better for development of all sectors including fisheries, and tourism, the PM said.

The second bill, the Reserve Bank National Credit Register Bill 2026 aims to improve the collection of accurate, timely, and relevant credit information to support lenders' credit risk assessments of borrowers and facilitate the NRBT 's oversight of financial institutions, the PM told the House.

Both bills passed their first readings, and were referred to joint standing committees, the Legislation Committee and the Finance & Public Accounts Committee for further scrutiny.

Meanwhile, nine annual ministerial reports for 2024-2025 were tabled into the House.

The annual reports were referred to the Whole House Committee.

Deputy PM Hon. Dr Viliami Latu expressed satisfaction with Team Tonga's performances at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games.

He reported to the House that Tonga won one medal, a bronze in Judo. This marks the first time in 16 years that Tonga won a medal at the Commonwealth Games.

He also noted it was the first time the national netball team, Tala, participated in the Commonwealth Games where they finished in 9th place.

Tevita Puloka, People's representative for Tongatapu No.1 reported on the development of community sports in his constituency. He also expressed concern for littering and crimes committed by young people. He said that together with the town officer, they were addressing these issues within the communities of Tongatapu 1.

Dr. ‘Aisake Eke, People's representative for Tongatapu No.5 said it was time to reflect on the lessons llearnt from the Commonwealth Games and identify areas for improvement in future competitions.

He said that Tonga's team had consistently faced challenges due to inadequate preparations and that better planning and training were needed. Looking ahead to the Pacific Games in 2031, he said he hoped Tonga would be better prepared. He added it was time for the country to strive for gold medals.

PM Lord Fakafanua reported to the House on the impact of the El Niño in Tonga.

He warned that the country's water supply has been severely affected with a drought declared in Ha’apai.

He told the House that a seawater desalination plant has been installed in Haʻafeva, Haʻapai, while the National Disaster Risk Management Office ( NDRMO ) has distributed water tanks and supplied drinking water throughout the Haʻapai island group.

The PM urged the public to use water wisely and collect as much rainwater as possible. He also advised the House that the current El Niño conditions are expected to continue until June 2027.

Saimone Vuki, People's representative for Haʻapai No.12 expressed concern about the water situation in his constituency. He reported that Lifuka currently has an adequate water supply. However, he warned that if the water tanks were to run dry, the situation would become much more serious.

He also reported that Koulo and Lopeka are experiencing problems with their water pumping systems, which require immediate repairs. In ʻUiha and Felemea, he said the water has become too salty for regular use. He further noted that the water supplies in Lofanga and Moʻungaʻone are expected to be significantly affected by the ongoing drought.

He told the House that one of the government's challenges is that water tanks are sometimes distributed to households that do not need them following government surveys. He urged the government to work more closely with local town officers to ensure that assistance is directed to the homes most in need. He urged that the national response to El Niño should be better coordinated.

' Esafe Latu, People's representative for Haʻapai No.13 requested that the government provide and distribute additional water tanks to affected communities.

Mateni Tapueluelu, People's representative for Tongatapu No.4 proposed that the House adjourn to allow the relevant committee to conduct meaningful meetings and for members to review the reports.

Fangaʻuta Lagoon Bridge and the commissioning of the new MEIDECC office at Matatoa

However, Piveni Piukala, People's representative for Tongatapu No.7 told the House that several construction in Tongatapu 7 had been issued stop orders by the Minister for Lands.

He also questioned the delays in the construction of the Fangaʻuta Lagoon Bridge and the commissioning of the new MEIDECC office at Matatoa.

Deputy PM Hon. Dr Viliami Latu criticized Piveni for discussing these matters on social media, saying that the information being circulated had caused confusion regarding the issues raised.

Responding to the concerns raised by Piveni, the PM said that the public concern surrounding the two government projects was largely "due to misinformation being circulated."

Regarding the Fangaʻuta Lagoon Bridge project, he said the government is still completing the necessary requirements to avoid future delays. He added that work on the project design is still ongoing. The construction was commissioned last year.
